rows.notes: Partner addresses AI1; educational metaphor and quote marks retained.

rows.en: Hm? The unit won't move...! What are you playing at?
rows.notes: Pilot challenges partner over immobilization.

rows.en: AI1 wants to watch whoever comes out from inside the absolute barrier...
rows.notes: Entity remains unspecified; emerging from barrier. Absolute barrier spelling confirmed centrally from RahXephon: Pluralitas Concentio.

rows.en: You're saying it took control of Medius just to do that?
rows.notes: It refers to AI1 taking control.

rows.en: ...Please, let the child do as it pleases.
rows.notes: Partner affectionately calls AI1 the child; neutral it avoids AI gender. No possessive added to the source reference.

rows.en: Don't be ridiculous. If you can't move on a battlefield, you're nothing but a target.
rows.notes: Pilot rebukes partner: immobilization makes their unit a target.

rows.en: Restore control immediately. Surely you don't intend to die here, either?
rows.notes: Pilot orders partner to restore control.

rows.en: What's this? That robot's looking toward TOKYO JUPITER.
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: ...Looking away in the middle of a fight? It must be feeling pretty confident.
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: But something seems wrong...
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: Wrong? What do you mean?
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: It's far too defenseless...
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: It's as though the robot itself is watching TOKYO JUPITER.
rows.notes: Robot itself appears to look, distinct from its pilot.

rows.en: Medius itself is... watching?
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: #男愛称, now's our chance!
rows.notes: Co-pilot urges protagonist to exploit Medius immobilization.

rows.en: Ugh!?
rows.notes: Pain vocalization retained.

rows.en: #男愛称!?
rows.notes: Name-only alarm retained.

rows.en: G-ghhh...!
rows.notes: Pain groan retained.

rows.en: #男愛称, what's wrong!?
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: My hands and feet are going numb...! That's impossible. It's too soon for that.
rows.notes: Protagonist thinks about premature numbness.

rows.en: #男愛称! What's wrong, #男愛称!?
rows.notes: Both repeated runtime nicknames retained.

rows.en: Is the medicine starting to wear off...!?
rows.notes: Stray closing thought wrapper in source body omitted; body only.

rows.en: This can't be happening. If I lose control of my hands and feet out here...!
rows.notes: Deliberately unfinished consequence retained; hands and feet both preserved.

rows.en: Hey, #男愛称! Keep the unit under control!
rows.notes: Co-pilot tells protagonist to pilot properly; control refers to their unit.

rows.en: Damn it, is this what Zapat was talking about...!?
rows.notes: Surname Zapat retained from Mitar Zapat; source does not say Mitar.

rows.en: What's happening!?
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: I'm reading high energy on the surface of TOKYO JUPITER's absolute barrier!
rows.notes: Torres reports energy at barrier surface, not within it. Absolute barrier spelling confirmed centrally from RahXephon: Pluralitas Concentio.

rows.en: A Dolem!? All units, stay alert!!
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: It's here...!
rows.notes: Hidden observer reacts to arriving entity; it has no inferred gender.

rows.en: Wh-what is that!?
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: Is that thing a Dolem!?
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: It has a human shape...!
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: More than that, it's almost like...!
rows.notes: Comparison deliberately trails off.
Pure shock punctuation retained.

rows.en: Th-that robot just roared!
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: I-it's like it...! Something about it reminds me of that one...!
rows.notes: Koji begins similarity comparison; next row identifies Raideen.

rows.en: Y-yeah...! Akira's Raideen...!
rows.notes: Ryoma completes comparison to Akira's Raideen; matching comparison fragment retained.

rows.en: I-it just took off!
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: What was that thing...!?
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: Wait, Ayato! Ayato!!
rows.notes: Haruka calls to Ayato twice; no honorific added.

rows.en: ...Was that humanoid what AI1 wanted to see?
rows.notes: Pilot retrospectively asks about humanoid AI1 observed.

rows.en: Yes.
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: ...What is that thing?
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: I don't know.
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: You don't know?
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: That's right. AI1 detected a quantum condensation reaction with its sensors... and simply said it wanted to come here.
rows.notes: Partner says AI1 detected reaction with sensors and requested this visit.
uncertain: Quantum condensation reaction is source-literal; no independently established canonical English technical name.

rows.en: Impossible. It wanted "knowledge" besides combat data? It... a mere artificial intelligence for controlling a unit...
rows.notes: Pilot incredulous that control AI sought noncombat knowledge; unfinished ending retained.

rows.en: More to the point... we've achieved our objective. I recommend that we withdraw from here.
rows.notes: Partner recommends their withdrawal after achieving observation objective.

rows.en: ...Understood.
rows.notes: Context follows adjacent battle-event exchange; subject and action restored where required.

rows.en: M-Medius...!
rows.notes: Name fragment retained; next row supplies escape action.

rows.en: It got away!?
rows.notes: Judau completes escape observation with explicit subject.

rows.en: #男愛称!
rows.notes: Name-only alarm retained.

rows.en: ...The numbness is easing. It looks like my medicine hasn't worn off...
rows.notes: Male lead's numbness is easing; medicine has apparently not worn off, no invented diagnosis.

rows.en: Are you all right!?
Yeah... We're going after Medius Locus.
Roger! We can still catch it! I'll get clearance from Captain Bright...
rows.notes: Aqua seeks Bright's clearance before pursuit; request trails off. Coordinator terminology correction: Akurasu Bright Noa profile explicitly maps his Char's Counterattack rank 大佐 to naval Captain. Earlier Colonel rendering was incorrect; full original draft retained.

rows.en: Captain Haruka Shitow! Shitow! Damn, did she go after that thing...!?
rows.notes: Elvy calls to Haruka; she refers to Haruka following the giant, not Medius.

rows.en: That's a TERRA fighter, right?
Yeah. So was the one we saw earlier.
Then Operation Overlord is...
rows.notes: Kaine trails off wondering about Operation Overlord.

rows.en: More high-energy readings on the surface of TOKYO JUPITER! A large number of them!
! Those Mu bastards followed me out!!
rows.notes: Elvy reacts to pursuit from Mu; first-person target restored from fighter context.

rows.en: Identification complete! According to TERRA's data, they're D2 Dotems!
rows.notes: D2 source classification retained; Dotem glossary form pluralized.

rows.en: Mu's small weapons, then! All units, commence attack! Cover the friendly fighter!
Captain Bright, what should we do!?
rows.notes: Aqua asks what she and male lead should do; verb restored. Coordinator terminology correction: Akurasu Bright Noa profile explicitly maps his Char's Counterattack rank 大佐 to naval Captain. Earlier Colonel rendering was incorrect; full original draft retained.

rows.en: Intercepting the Dotems takes priority now! We'll leave the pursuit of Medius to other units!
U-understood!
Damn it! If only there was nothing wrong with my body...!
rows.notes: Male lead wishes his physical problem had not interfered; conditional intentionally trails off.

rows.en: 1. Shinsei Type II is shot down@2. Mothership is shot down
rows.notes: Plain defeat conditions preserve one @; each segment checked against 352 px.

rows.en: The Dotem readings have disappeared. There's no sign of enemy reinforcements from TOKYO JUPITER either.
I see. What about the TERRA fighter?
It's intact. We're receiving a transmission from it.
Captain Bright, I'm Lieutenant Elvy Hadhiyat. Thank you for your support earlier.
rows.notes: Elvy formally introduces herself as a lieutenant, despite general glossary position of captain; source rank wins here. Coordinator terminology correction: Akurasu Bright Noa profile explicitly maps his Char's Counterattack rank 大佐 to naval Captain. Earlier Colonel rendering was incorrect; full original draft retained.

rows.en: Lieutenant, what happened to the other units that entered TOKYO JUPITER?
...They were all wiped out... except for me and Captain Haruka Shitow.
rows.notes: Elvy excludes only herself and Captain Haruka from the wiped-out force.

rows.en: ...I see.
I'll return to my mothership, then.
Bright...
Yes... To think they were all wiped out...
rows.notes: Bright reacts to the total losses; to think preserves his stunned reaction without inventing a separate disbelief statement.

rows.en: Operation Overlord... Could its true objective have been that giant...?
rows.notes: Bright questions whether the giant was the true objective; no invented recovery/capture action.

rows.en: W-what's happening!?
We're getting strong Mutron energy readings from Raideen at Divine Face Rock...!
rows.notes: Divine Face Rock and Mutron follow glossary; report predicate supplied.

rows.en: Th-that can't be! Akira hasn't even faded in!
rows.notes: fade-in is the Raideen pilot-merge technique; used naturally as verb.

rows.en: ...What do you think, Dr. Hibiki?
Hmm... This is like the first time Raideen appeared before us.
Don't tell me it's the Demon Empire!?
rows.notes: Mari fears a Demon Empire return; question preserved without asserting one.

rows.en: That's impossible! I defeated Great Demon Emperor Barao!
At a terrible cost... Jinguji and my mother...!!
rows.notes: Continuing cost phrase from Akira's previous row; casualties include Jinguji and his mother. Root confirmed Jinguji surname via Akurasu Compact Pilot Database; no first name added.

rows.en: Akira is right. Barao and Demon Island were certainly destroyed that day...
rows.notes: Demon Island provisional pending centralized glossary research. Root approved provisional literal wording, matching Demon Empire.
uncertain: Demon Island is provisional literal wording; no canonical English entry established.

rows.en: By Raideen and Akira, who had gained the light of the Star of Ra Mu.
rows.notes: Continues by-phrase from 517; Akira/Raideen victory with Star of Ra Mu retained.

rows.en: I'm sorry... I didn't think about how you must feel, Akira, after losing your mother in that battle...
rows.notes: Mari apologizes to Akira for failing to consider his grief.

rows.en: ...No, it's all right... Mari.
Hmm... The energy readings have subsided.
What on earth happened to Raideen?
It may be giving us a warning, just like it did back then.
A warning... Akira, what did you feel?
I'm sure Raideen was trying to tell us something, but what it was...
rows.notes: Akira knows a message was intended but not its content; source trailing boundary retained.

rows.en: ...Akira, prepare to launch, just in case. You too, Mari, please.
rows.notes: Dr. Hibiki asks both Akira and Mari to prepare; request direction preserved.

rows.en: Understood, Dad. ...Mari, let's go.
Y-yeah...
...Higashiyama, this may be connected to what Dr. Kisaragi of TERRA told us.
Hmm. It also worries me that this happened at the same time as Operation Overlord...
Did Dr. Kisaragi foresee this when he asked us to develop the RMU system...?
rows.notes: RMU acronym is not expanded; Dr. Kisaragi is Itsuki in TERRA context. Root approved source-literal RMU system; no expansion.

rows.en: Yes. And so did the Bahbem Foundation, with all their persistent requests to investigate Raideen.
rows.notes: Bahbem Foundation likewise anticipated events; investigation requests concern Raideen.

rows.en: There does seem to be some connection between Raideen and that OOPArts...
rows.notes: OOPArts retains glossary capitalization; refers to the previously discussed artifact.

rows.en: ...It seems your operation went well.
Yes. Every Dotem successfully penetrated the barrier.
If it's possible to enter this Tokyo, then the reverse is also true...
rows.notes: Kuki observes barrier transit works in reverse; no invented physics.

rows.en: By applying TERRA's system, we can use the Dolems to conquer the outside world by force.
...If that's what you would call conquest.
rows.notes: Maya questions the description as conquest; if-fragment retained.

rows.en: Lady Maya... Why do you hesitate at this stage?
...As I thought, this man doesn't understand Lady Maya's thinking at all...
rows.notes: Miwa refers to Kuki, established by adjacent dialogue; sourced male gender from glossary.

rows.en: Kuki, if you heard Miwa's report, you should understand how much energy it takes to form a corridor to the outside...
rows.notes: Maya answers Kuki using Miwa's corridor-energy report; subject and causal condition explicit.

rows.en: If we send out enough forces to fight the outside powers on equal terms, it will have a major impact on our side too, you know?
rows.notes: Deploying forces sufficient to match outside powers would harm their own side; vague effect kept as source.

rows.en: That is true, but...
For now, Ayato will be our only target.
rows.notes: Maya limits their current target to Ayato.

rows.en: Are you sure that's all we should do?
It was my mistake to let Ayato get outside...
Even though he's seventeen now, I didn't think he had grown enough to pilot Xephon.
rows.notes: Seventeen refers to Ayato's age, not an elapsed duration.

rows.en: I also thought Xephon would never allow him to leave Tokyo.
rows.notes: Xephon as grammatical subject of permitting Ayato's exit retained; possible alternative subject/object parse flagged. Root reviewed 545-548 and confirmed this follows the explicit ga subject and causative exit wording; no rewrite of source particle.

rows.en: ...But this incident may give Ayato a good opportunity to grow.
Exposure to the outside world and its trials should bring him closer to awakening as an Instrumentalist.
rows.notes: Trials are to awaken Ayato as an Instrumentalist; title follows glossary.

rows.en: What will we do about TERRA?
They must be planning the same thing... Surely it's only natural for us to lend them a hand?
rows.notes: Maya proposes helping TERRA advance the same awakening plan, with dry rhetorical tone.

rows.en: But wouldn't that put the people synchronized with the Dolems in danger?
rows.notes: Miwa refers to the people synchronized with Dolems; no inferred gender.

rows.en: What do two or three Mulians matter? If necessary, I don't mind losing a thousand of our people.
rows.notes: Maya accepts losing two/three or even one thousand fellow Mulians; full severity retained.

rows.en: ...Lady Maya's resolve goes that far...
rows.notes: Miwa's thought registers Maya's determination; source trailing thought retained.

rows.en: But beyond the barrier lies the other side's legacy of Mu. Wouldn't contact between it and Xephon be dangerous?
rows.notes: Other side's Mu legacy left unspecified; contact risk not explained beyond source.

rows.en: It's safe for now... Their Conductor has not yet awakened.
rows.notes: Conductor title provisional pending centralized research; their referent deliberately not named. Root confirmed literal title; their Conductor remains unidentified.
uncertain: Conductor is a source-literal title; no independently established canonical English entry.

rows.en: Yes...
Is that clear? Do not forget that Ayato's awakening is the very purpose of our plan, and our deepest wish.
...5A is currently secured to this ship's deck. So far, we have observed no abnormalities.
I see.
Still, it's remarkable that you managed to guide that thing aboard the Lilia Litvyak.
Yes... We have Captain Haruka Shitow to thank for that, Inspector Makoto Isshiki.
Heh... It's a twist of fate.
rows.notes: Fatalistic remark; complete clause restores source grammatical subject/copula. Personal connection deliberately unspecified.

rows.en: What do you mean?
Nothing. I was talking to myself. Pay it no mind.
...He's supposedly an inspector sent by the Federation government to investigate TERRA's activities, but...
rows.notes: Thought continues into569; Federation inspector cover contrasted with Foundation allegiance.

rows.en: He's working for the Foundation, all right.
rows.notes: Foundation is Bahbem Foundation from sourced Isshiki affiliation; source short form preserved.

rows.en: Now then... What new information have you learned about 5A?
Nothing of note at present. Dr. Itsuki Kisaragi will conduct a detailed investigation once we return to Nirai Kanai.
Itsuki...
Oh, right... There was one thing we learned.
rows.notes: Self-correction about finding one new piece of information retained.

rows.en: What is it?
5A's name. That boy called it "RahXephon."
rows.notes: 5A source short designation retained; RahXephon quoted as its name.

rows.en: Heh... He's like a child naming a toy he's just bought.
Where is the boy now?
His examination just finished. Would you like to see him?
...Yes, I would.
...Why did I have to take a blood test just to come aboard this ship?
Well, you see... It's just a formality.
...My blood was red, you know.
Y-yes...
And another thing, Shitow...
rows.notes: Ayato uses Haruka's surname; following line invites first-name address.

rows.en: Just call me Haruka. I'll call you Ayato in return. ...Now, what is it?
rows.notes: Mutual first-name address direction preserved.

rows.en: Where is this ship headed?
We're going to Nirai Kanai.
...Nirai Kanai... If I remember correctly, it means "the island where the gods live" in Okinawan, right?
rows.notes: Meaning of Nirai Kanai translated as the character's explanation, not independently asserted geography.

rows.en: You know your stuff. But that island isn't where the gods live, and it isn't in Okinawa either.
It's an experimental city at sea, built by adding an artificial island to Negoro Island off the coast of Kyushu.
rows.notes: Negoro Island glossary spelling retained with provenance gap. Source artificial-island addition does not establish multiple islands.
uncertain: Unsourced glossary spelling Negoro Island retained.

rows.en: Experimental...? Does that have something to do with Tokyo... what you call TOKYO JUPITER?
Yes. And that island is also home to TERRA's headquarters.
TERRA...?
Yes. TERRA is an anti-MU strategy research agency. We investigate why MU invaded and develop countermeasures.
rows.notes: Only measured overflow compressed: retains anti-MU strategy research role, invasion cause investigation and countermeasure development.

rows.en: Who are you?
I'm Jin Kunugi, commander of TERRA.
The commander...
rows.notes: Source repetition of commander title retained.

rows.en: Ayato Kamina... No official decision has yet been made on how you will be treated.
Therefore, until this ship arrives at Nirai Kanai, your movements aboard it will be restricted. Bear that in mind.
And before you forget, you should reset the time on your watch.
rows.notes: Watch reset command continues with qualifier in601.

rows.en: ...To the correct time.
rows.notes: Qualifier continues600 across row boundary.

rows.en: What do you mean?
...Captain Shitow, escort him to his assigned room, then report to the bridge.
Huh...?
You heard me, didn't you?
Yes...
That will be all.
What's with his attitude...?
Well... He can be a little difficult, but he's not a bad person.
More to the point, what did he mean by the correct time?
Back in Tokyo, you said you'd tell me everything about the world...
rows.notes: Source trailing assertion retained.

rows.en: What is this world, anyway? Wasn't the whole world destroyed by the invaders' attacks, with only Tokyo left?
...Ayato... Do you know how many people live in the world now?
Until yesterday, I thought it was twenty-three million.
I see... But in this world, including the space colonies, there are nearly ten billion people.
You're seventeen now, right? Do you know what year this is?
Space Era 76...
rows.notes: Root approved Space Era for this source calendar; dates 76/89 exact. Not conflated with Universal Century.

rows.en: ...Stay calm and listen. It's Space Era 89 now.
rows.notes: Root approved Space Era for this source calendar; dates 76/89 exact. Not conflated with Universal Century.

rows.en: Wh-what?!
Look at my watch. It has two time displays, see?
...The top one shows the time in our world. The bottom one shows the time in Tokyo.
Wh-what do you mean?
Time flows differently inside TOKYO JUPITER than it does outside...
One second there is six seconds here. One year there is six years here.
rows.notes: Six-to-one time ratio preserved in both seconds and years.

rows.en: That's a lie...! How could something like that happen?!
The physics are far too complicated for me to explain. But this is reality.
Then the outside world...?!
rows.notes: Unfinished question retained; subsequent historical explanation answers it.

rows.en: The war you call the Invasion War... the one in which the invaders destroyed the world... We call it the Mu War.
rows.notes: Root approved source-literal Invasion War contrasted with Mu War; no First added.

rows.en: Mu?
Fifteen years ago, something like a floating city appeared in the sky over Tokyo.
The people inside it only identified themselves as MU. They never responded to our attempts to contact them.
...They didn't attack us. They just stayed there... To us, their presence was unnerving.
So people at the time imagined there must be something behind it.
Then humanity was overwhelmed by the nightmare it had imagined, and launched an attack on MU's floating city...
rows.notes: Humanity initiates the attack, driven by its own imagined fear; not MU aggression.

rows.en: What did MU do?
Naturally, they fought back. With enormous weapons called Dolems.
Dolems... Those must be the things I fought in Tokyo.
rows.notes: Thought identifies the enemies Ayato fought in Tokyo.

rows.en: And in just one day, city after city was annihilated. As humanity braced for an all-out war with MU...
rows.notes: Deliberate unfinished temporal clause continues into639.

rows.en: Suddenly, a spherical dimensional barrier covered Tokyo, and MU shut themselves inside it.
rows.notes: MU retreat behind spherical dimensional barrier follows humanity preparing for full war.

rows.en: After that, Mu and humanity cut off all contact... Fifteen years passed out here, and just over two years passed in Tokyo.
rows.notes: Haruka describes time disparity:15 years outside, just over2 inside; Mu vs humanity.

rows.en: But the really hard part came after TOKYO JUPITER appeared...
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: Second Impact, the One Year War, the Lizard War... Out here, one event after another shook the entire Earth Sphere.
rows.notes: Historical events preserved using glossary names; Lizard War short dialogue form.

rows.en: People even said Mu knew those things were coming, and that's why they shut themselves inside the absolute barrier.
rows.notes: Reported speculation, not established fact; Mu plural group pronoun.

rows.en: But... you'd spent fifteen years leaving Tokyo alone... So why did you try to bring me out, Haruka?
rows.notes: Ayato asks why Haruka extracted him after15 years of leaving Tokyo alone.

rows.en: Because those were my orders... I don't know the details myself.
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: ...Just tell me one thing... My mom and my friends are still there, right...?
rows.notes: Question begins with mother/friends existence; reply expands in647.

rows.en: Beyond that wall... in TOKYO JUPITER... They're alive there, aren't they?
rows.notes: Alive question remains tentative; plural they identified in preceding row.

rows.en: Yes...
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: ...They're alive...
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: ...That's all for now, Ayato. I'm going to take you to a certain room.
rows.notes: Haruka closes history discussion and sends Ayato to detention room.

rows.en: Is that the one that man Kunugi was talking about...?
rows.notes: Ayato asks about room mentioned by Kunugi; surname retained.

rows.en: Yes... That's right.
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: Captain Haruka Shitow...
rows.notes: Elvy addresses Haruka by full name and Captain rank.
Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: What's wrong?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: Sorry, but go on ahead. Just keep going straight and you'll get there.
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: Huh?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: We have something a little complicated to discuss. Just us girls.
rows.notes: Private conversation with Elvy, female gender sourced from glossary.

rows.en: O-okay...
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: I see. That absinthe you treated me to when we first met has turned out to be pretty expensive.
rows.notes: Absinthe treats cost as metaphor for Elvy battlefield losses and apparent manipulation; retain sarcasm.

rows.en: I heard you were the only one to go inside and make it back alive. Impressive, First Lieutenant Hadhiyat.
rows.notes: Haruka addresses Elvy by surname/rank; praises sole return from TOKYO JUPITER.

rows.en: Captain Shitow, I'm asking this knowing you're in intelligence. A yes or no will do.
rows.notes: Elvy demands yes/no despite Haruka intelligence role.

rows.en: Just so you know, I didn't get a receipt for our drinks that day. It's true.
rows.notes: Receipt remark answers absinthe metaphor and deflects question; no reimbursement explanation added.

rows.en: ...Did you know the full scope of Operation Overlord, too?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: Was that worthless boy what we got in exchange for my comrades' blood?
rows.notes: Elvy contempt toward Ayato retained as worthless boy; her comrades blood is cost.

rows.en: Where did you hear that?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: What I want to know is whether you knew what this operation was about!
rows.notes: Elvy repeats demand toward Haruka; no softer wording.

rows.en: ...Looks like our trip to the Chinese restaurant next week is off.
rows.notes: Haruka anticipates cancellation of shared Chinese meal; no explicit answer invented.
Pure shock retained; no slap narration added.

rows.en: ...Am I really going the right way...? Hm? What's that...?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: Oh, it's a barbershop. They have one of those inside an aircraft carrier. It even has a sign...
rows.notes: Ayato discovers onboard barbershop, then its sign.

rows.en: That sign was originally used to mark a field hospital.
rows.notes: Quon states in-world historical claim; no external factual correction.

rows.en: The red and blue stripes? ...Actually, who are you?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: ...They say those colors represent red blood vessels and blue blood vessels.
rows.notes: Red/blue blood-vessel explanation preserves source words, no arteries/veins explanation inserted.

rows.en: I-is that so?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: Even though human blood is red...
rows.notes: Quon deliberate unfinished observation retained.

rows.en: Hm?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: Why do we have blood vessels in two different colors...?
rows.notes: Quon question has explicit subject/action rather than noun fragment.

rows.en: Two colors... Red blood and blue blood...
rows.notes: Ayato echoes two-color phrase in thoughts; deliberate noun fragment retained.

rows.en: ...Mom was definitely bleeding blue blood back then...
rows.notes: Ayato remembers mother blue blood; her gender from mother relationship.

rows.en: Let's go, Ollin.
rows.notes: Ollin glossary spelling; Quon calls Ayato.

rows.en: Huh? Um... What's an Ollin?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: It doesn't matter.
rows.notes: Quon dismisses question; context settles it as name explanation.

rows.en: H-hey, wait a second!
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: What's going on, Commander!? Ayato's room... That's a detention cell designed for Mulians, isn't it!?

rows.notes: Any attempted forced opening kills occupant; opener left unspecified.

rows.en: ...The analysis results for the biomolecular markers are in.

uncertain: Source-literal scientific label; no independently established canonical English technical wording.

rows.en: Whatever else he may be, he's a human with red blood, just like us!
rows.notes: Haruka explicitly insists Ayato is red-blooded human like them.

rows.notes: Kunugi says human/red-blooded condition holds only for now; restore subject/verb.

rows.en: Footage...? Of what?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: Of the robot that came out of TOKYO JUPITER back then.
rows.notes: Koji identifies footage object from prior battle.

rows.en: ...So, what did you say that thing looked like?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: Actually, Demon Bird Si...
rows.notes: Akurasu-sourced Sirene reference; preserve Demon Bird Si... cutoff, not complete name. Following sky-attack joke retained.

rows.en: If you say any more, we'll get attacked from the sky.

rows.en: What are you talking about?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: Well... The robot it reminds us of is Raideen.

rows.en: That's the one that fought the Demon Empire, isn't it...?
rows.notes: Iino checks remembered Demon Empire association.

rows.en: Yes. It's a legacy of the ancient Mu Empire, a robot powered by Mutron.
rows.notes: Ancient Mu Empire distinct from RahXephon Mu; Raideen powered by Mutron.

rows.en: What's the Mu Empire? Where is it?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: It was a country that flourished about ten thousand years ago, but natural disasters sank it beneath the sea.
rows.notes: Michiru explains extinct country and catastrophic sinking, no additional continent label.

rows.en: Hm? Does that mean... Raideen might actually be a robot from ancient times?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: That's right.
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: Huh... I can't believe they built something like that so long ago.
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: It's not so strange. The Mechanical Beasts I used to fight were originally giant warriors dug up from ancient ruins.
rows.notes: Koji relates Mechanical Beasts to excavated ancient giant warriors.

rows.en: Don't you get the feeling technology used to be more amazing than it is now?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: You can say that again.
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: By the way, Ryo... When's Akira coming to join our unit?
rows.notes: Ryo is source nickname for Ryoma; Akira glossary spelling.

rows.en: Director Higashiyama just contacted me... Apparently, he'll be a little later than planned.
rows.notes: Director Higashiyama update concerns Akira arrival.

rows.en: I see... I wonder if something happened at Mutropolis?
rows.notes: Adjacent dialogue settles speaker/listener and referent; English retains complete subject/action.

rows.en: ...Getting back to what we were saying... Why did you think that robot looked like Raideen?
rows.notes: Light returns discussion to reason for robot/Raideen similarity.

rows.en: Well, those of us who've fought alongside Raideen can just sort of tell...
rows.notes: Ryoma attributes recognition to team experience alongside Raideen; continuation720 clarifies aura.

rows.en: That robot has a distinctive presence that reminds us of Raideen.
In other words, the two are closely related in their very nature.
rows.notes: Nature/existence affinity to Raideen, not a confirmed shared manufacturing origin.

rows.en: Then maybe that robot is from ancient times too.
Hey, guys! We've got big news!
What's up, Kaine? Did Linda finally send you an email?
rows.notes: Linda provisional missing-glossary spelling; source727 explicitly calls her a girl. Root confirmed short Linda from Akurasu Linda Plato entry; no surname added.

rows.en: No, I haven't heard a thing from her. Maybe she's forgotten all about me.
Hey, hey, who's Linda?
rows.notes: Root confirmed short Linda from Akurasu Linda Plato entry; no surname added.

rows.en: She's a girl who was on our ship until we came down to Earth... and Kaine has an unrequited crush on her.
rows.notes: Female gender grounded in explicit source girl, not name inference. Root confirmed short Linda from Akurasu Linda Plato entry; no surname added.

rows.en: Shut up! Just you watch! One day, she'll love me back!
Why are you getting so worked up?
So what's the big news, anyway?
Oh, right! That robot from before is on the Li... Li... Li... Li...
rows.notes: Kaine forgets Lilia Litvyak name; repeated Li syllable retained.

rows.en: Huh? Is that a cricket chirping?
rows.notes: Cricket guess follows repeated Li chirping sound; localized as chirping cricket.

rows.en: Nah, that's a runner taking a lead off first, right?
rows.notes: Baseball guess clarified as runner taking a lead off first; Li/lead sound joke only partly transfers into English.
uncertain: First-base lead wordplay only partly carries through English.

rows.en: No! You know, the Li... Li... Argh, I can't remember!
You mean the Lilia Litvyak, right? TERRA's aircraft carrier...
rows.notes: Lilia Litvyak glossary name; aircraft-carrier descriptor trails off.

rows.en: That's it! Apparently, they brought that robot aboard it.
What did you say...?
Then was the real purpose of Operation Overlord to bring that thing out of Tokyo?
rows.notes: Question infers operation purpose from news; no certainty inserted.

rows.en: Yeah, that's what it looks like.
Good grief... They brought out not just us, but the Federation's fleet and ground forces too.
So the mountain shook, and all that came out was one mouse.
rows.notes: Mountain-and-mouse proverb retained so742 can explicitly answer its mouse metaphor.

rows.en: It's no ordinary mouse. It's a robot they were willing to drag us out there to get...
You can bet there's some important secret hidden in it.
#男愛称, are you all right?
rows.notes: Honorific dropped; runtime nickname preserved.

rows.en: Yeah... I'm fine now.
But what on earth happened to you?
It's just a little episode, or something like that. Sometimes my arms and legs go numb, and I can't move them.
rows.notes: Medical attack described as episode rather than diagnosing a seizure; symptoms explicitly numbness and inability to move limbs.

rows.en: ...An episode...
rows.notes: Thought repeats episode term used in747; no seizure diagnosis implied.

rows.en: A little? Sometimes? You've got to be kidding! We let the Medius get away because of you!

uncertain: Silent ……… rendered '...'. The line is reused in i00r0a:3/16/62/97 (the interlude), so it is a neutral silence.

rows.en: Besides, this is the first I've heard of you having a chronic condition like that. Why didn't you tell me before now?
...Because there was no need to tell you.
Don't give me that! You said you'd handle piloting #機体名 and the fighting...
rows.notes: Female lead quotes male lead's earlier promise; quote rendered as second-person reported speech. Trailing clause continues753.

rows.en: But you were carrying a ticking time bomb all along? That's no joke!
rows.notes: Bomb is metaphor for concealed medical condition; no literal explosive claimed.

rows.en: I can't believe you've been a pilot with your body in that condition!
It's not like I wanted my body to end up this way.
rows.notes: Private thought, not spoken retort.

rows.en: #女愛称, I don't really know what's going on, but... Don't you think that was going a little too far?
I... think so too.
rows.notes: Stray closing quote and @ ignored per source-cleanup convention.

rows.en: Ah... Y-you're right. I'm sorry, #男愛称.
rows.notes: Stray closing quote and @ ignored; nickname retained.

rows.en: I'm not upset. Besides, it's my fault the Medius got away. I'm sorry.
rows.notes: Male lead accepts responsibility for Medius escape; apology direction preserved.
Silence retained; stray trailing source wrapper ignored.

rows.en: What's wrong?
Nothing. Never mind.
I thought he was younger than me but had no charm at all... Maybe that's not really true.
rows.notes: Female lead privately reassesses younger male lead; sourced gender from runtime male lead role.

rows.en: #男愛称, for now, would you please let the doctor examine you and run some detailed tests?
rows.notes: Leina requests examination/tests; no exact diagnosis invented.

rows.en: No, I'm fine.
Come on, you should get checked just to be safe. If it happens again, it could get you killed.
I... know that.
Then why won't you let the doctor examine you? Don't tell me you're scared of needles?
rows.notes: Female lead teasingly asks whether needles frighten male lead.

rows.en: I'm more scared of an older woman who won't stop nagging me.
rows.notes: Male lead jokes back about nagging older woman; comparative fear preserved.

rows.en: Wh-what...?!
I take it back! He really has no charm at all!
rows.notes: Callback reverses thought763.

rows.en: Then, #男愛称... At least let me get you some medicine.
rows.notes: Source omits offered action; medicine is offered after doctor-exam refusal, restored as get medicine.

rows.en: I've got my own. ...Sorry for making you all worry so much.
Hey, wait! #男愛称!
...Is #男愛称 really going to be all right?
rows.notes: Judau asks about lead after lead leaves; nickname third-person subject.

rows.en: Unless he lets the doctor examine him, I can't tell how he's really doing.
Those symptoms... Could they be...
rows.notes: Unfinished private inference continues into778.

rows.en: Could they be side effects of muscle enhancers or painkillers for the nervous system...?
rows.notes: Muscle enhancers and nervous-system analgesics are source-literal classes; no diagnosis/real drug name added.

rows.en: But that shouldn't happen unless the dose is enormous... or the drug itself is extremely potent...
rows.notes: Large dose or high potency required for suspected side effects; preserves alternative conditions.

rows.en: Patrol duty in the Japan region?
Yes... Far East Command headquarters asked me to help, taking the Vegan Empire attacks and Dolem appearance seriously.
rows.notes: Only measured overflow compressed. Root approved source-literal Far East Command headquarters; Dolem corrects context-settled source typo. No OG organization equivalence claimed.

rows.en: What about our mission to transport the D-Weapons?
Chongqing Base isn't fully prepared to receive them yet...
And the General Staff have told me they want you to buy them some more time.
...Understood. Then we'll cooperate with Far East Command and take up patrol duty in the Japan region.
rows.notes: Root approved source-literal Far East Command; source here does not add headquarters. No canonical MX English label asserted.

rows.en: Yes. I'm counting on you.
